hints: Focus on how the strength of the oxidising conditions changes what happens to the C=C double bond, mild addition versus full cleavage.
Cold, dilute KMnO4 adds two OH groups across the double bond, so cyclohexene keeps its ring and becomes a diol.
Hot, concentrated KMnO4 breaks the ring open at the double bond and oxidises both ends fully, so look for the open-chain dicarboxylic acid with six carbons.
walkthrough:
**Recall mild oxidation with cold, dilute KMnO4**

Think of this as gentle hydroxylation. The pi bond is broken, but the sigma skeleton stays together.

$$\text{cyclohexene} + [O] + \text{H}_2\text{O} \xrightarrow{\text{cold, dilute } \text{MnO}_4^-} \text{cyclohexane-1,2-diol}$$

**Picture the diol product**

The two carbons that were $\text{C=C}$ each gain one $\text{-OH}$ group. The six-membered ring is still intact.

That is 1,2-dihydroxycyclohexane, a vicinal diol.

**Recall vigorous oxidation with hot, concentrated KMnO4**

This is oxidative cleavage. The $\text{C=C}$ bond is completely broken and each alkene carbon is oxidised to its highest state.

$$\text{R-CH=CH-R'} \xrightarrow{\text{hot, conc. } \text{MnO}_4^-} \text{carboxylic acids}$$

**Apply cleavage to cyclohexene**

Because the double bond is in a ring, breaking it opens the ring. Both ends become $\text{-COOH}$ groups.

A 6-carbon ring opened this way gives $\text{HOOC-(CH}_2\text{)}_4\text{-COOH}$, which is hexanedioic acid. This matches only the row with diol under mild conditions and diacid under vigorous conditions.

options.A: Correct. Cold, dilute gives cyclohexane-1,2-diol with the ring intact. Hot, concentrated cleaves the ring to give hexanedioic acid, HOOC(CH2)4COOH. This correctly shows mild syn-dihydroxylation versus vigorous cleavage to carboxylic acids.
options.B: Swapped around. The diacid cannot form under cold, dilute conditions because cleavage needs vigorous heating and concentrated oxidant. The diol cannot survive hot, concentrated conditions because it would be further oxidised and cleaved.
options.C: Incorrect on both sides. Cold KMnO4 does not give a 1,2-diketone, it adds OH groups to make a diol. Hot KMnO4 does not stop at aldehydes, aldehydes are further oxidised to carboxylic acids under these strongly oxidising, hot conditions.
options.D: Incorrect on both sides. The dialdehyde shown for cold conditions implies cleavage, which does not happen with mild reagent. The diketone shown for hot conditions keeps the ring intact, but hot concentrated KMnO4 must break the C-C bond and open the ring.
